title: What planners, finance and regulators need

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: In an optimized plan, project W2 has the best NPV per dollar of all the projects left out. Its planner asks why it is not funded. Following the lesson, what kind of answer should the planner get?

options.text: A reason from the model's rows, like an alternative already in
options.says: Right: a ratio cannot explain a selection; only the model's rows can, as with P002, out because its alternative P001 is in.

options.text: Its NPV per dollar, since the ratio is all a selection depends on
options.says: P002 had the best ratio of the unfunded projects and was still out: the ratio does not decide.

options.text: No answer, since a plan proven optimal needs no further reason
options.says: The planner's real requirement is a reason for every project in terms of the rules, optimal plan or not.

options.text: The solver's gap, since a gap hides the best projects from the plan
options.says: The base plan was OPTIMAL with a gap tolerance of 0, and P002 was still out, because of its alternative row.

origin.section: Planners Need a Plan They Can Act On and Explain

questions.stem: A plan spends $300k less than the five yearly budgets add up to, and finance still rejects it. Following the lesson, which of finance's requirements can the plan have broken?

options.text: Its NPV must be computed at the regulator's allowed return
options.says: Finance wants NPV at the company's discount rate (lesson 7.2.1); the allowed return belongs to the revenue requirement.

options.text: It must use every dollar of each year's budget, leaving none
options.says: GridCap's accepted plan leaves $600k unspent; whole projects rarely use a year's last dollars.

options.text: Each year must be within its own budget, not only the total
options.says: Right: a plan within its five-year total can still break a year, and budgets are authorized year by year.

options.text: Its total spend must equal the NPV of the funded projects
options.says: Spend must add up to the funded projects' capex, spread by their cost profiles; NPV is a different number.

origin.section: Finance Needs Spend by Year That Matches What Was Authorized

questions.stem: An auditor reruns a plan of record from its stored inputs, using a newer solver release and eight threads. The rerun returns a different plan with exactly the same NPV. Following the lesson, what does this show?

options.text: The stored plan was not optimal, since the two plans differ
options.says: Both have the same NPV: a model can have several optimal plans, and a different one is not by itself an error.

options.text: The snapshot fixed the inputs, but not the software and settings
options.says: Right: threads, time limits and solver versions are what a snapshot alone does not fix.

options.text: The rerun is invalid, since every rerun must give the same plan
options.says: A rerun with other software and settings can return another optimal plan; the run manifest records what must match.

options.text: The inputs were edited, since a snapshot always fixes the plan
options.says: The snapshot fixes the inputs only; the lesson lists what it does not fix.

origin.section: Regulators Need Commitments Kept and a Result Anyone Can Reproduce
